children: Italian EU-harmonised consumer prices (HICP) rose 0.1% in August from the month before, with the annual inflation rate accelerating to 3.2% from July's 2.9%, preliminary data showed on Tuesday, amid high energy costs due to turmoil in the Middle East.
The reading was below a median forecast in a Reuters survey of 18 analysts, which pointed to a year-on-year rise of 3.4% and a month-on-month increase of 0.3%.
Official statistics agency ISTAT also reported that the main domestic price index (NIC) was up 0.5% month-on-month in August and up 3.3% annually, following a 2.9% annual rate in July.
The lower month-on-month rise for the HICP was due to seasonal summer sales for clothes and footwear, ISTAT said. The NIC index excludes temporary discounts.
Core inflation (net of fresh food and energy) was running at 1.4% year-on-year on the HICP index in August, decelerating from 1.6% in July.
